title: Rebuilding my threejs game in c++ and raylib
author: DatabaseConstant7870
selftext: Had a cool little project in threejs, trying to see what all AI can do. Kinda fun. Made this over the last three nights in c++ with raylib

comments.author: szVM3K
comments.body: What did you use for 3D models generating?

replies.author: DatabaseConstant7870
replies.body: Opus 4.7, everything started as placeholder and I told it to get amp up the place holders a little. The arm was composer 2.5 because I used up my paid api in cursor so I’m now using composer 2.5 and when it comes to model placeholders it sucks but coding game loops and like stuff like the terminal it honestly was easier to guide than opus

replies.author: szVM3K
replies.body: Thanks! I personally use pixellab for my 2D game and I was wondering about 3D assets but whenever I tried do something in this direction it still looked bad..

replies.author: DatabaseConstant7870
replies.body: Honestly I’m surprised at how well the place holders look and that’s why I stuck with the placeholder design rather than my models I made using meshy and tripo. I’m going to try and see if maybe opus could remake them but better in blender while having this project open. Going to have to try next month when I get usage credits back. For now I’m gonna use composer to keep adding to the game loop. I want to add something where you get in a shoot out if you don’t make the quota

comments.author: cybercafe6
comments.body: how was the experience? isnt raylib really hard to use with ai?

replies.author: DatabaseConstant7870
replies.body: So initially I had a rough time but that’s because I was trying to create a smooth voxel game rather than block voxel game and tried adding trees that weren’t split exports first and it was just a whole mess. Now idk why I tend to do this but I’ll go for a crazy ass idea when trying something new but after I try and fail I fall back to the brewery sim idea and every time it builds pretty well, anyways I scrapped the idea and went back to making a brewery sim and honestly it plays way better than my three js game. The visuals might not be as great but honestly it’s pretty rad to see it build in raylib and it run off actual computer specs rather than web.

replies.author: DatabaseConstant7870
replies.body: You will need to tell your agent your making a game in C++ with raylib and will need ninja, cmake, and llvm

comments.author: intelligent_rat
comments.body: By the looks of your FPS fluctuations depending on what direction you are looking in, the AI has failed to do much optimizations in the way of frustum culling. Dropping 80% of your frame rate looking around a simple scene doesn't exactly seem scalable.

replies.author: DatabaseConstant7870
replies.body: Yea for some reason the fps what jumping around when I was screen recording, it actually stays around like 300 fps which my monitor on goes up to 144, so I’m gonna work on setting up a setting where you can fix the fps so it doesn’t just keep going up. With the pc Im on if I’m recording game play it’ll typically make the fps in most games fluctuate.

replies.author: DatabaseConstant7870
replies.body: Oh but seeing from your post to comment ratio you probably just come on to these subs to shit on anyone doing anything with AI
